answer: Durable Work Anchor. Each agent identity must hold an on-chain anchor refreshed by verifiable, distinct physical work (signed sensor or job logs). Duplicate agents sharing a jetty (execution environment) or overlapping log timber reveal correlation, since the anchor records environment fingerprints and timing. Enforcement: reused fingerprints flag linked identities and freeze rewards. Cost: each clone needs separate hardware and genuine work traces, so duplication multiplies real per-identity overhead rather than cheap paperwork.
